articles.title: Unitree shares down 53% from IPO debut
articles.summary: Unitree Robotics shares have fallen about 39% from their first-day close and 53% from their debut-day high, reducing its valuation from a peak near $66 billion to roughly $30 billion. The company has meaningful revenue, including $252 million in 2025 and more than 5,500 humanoid shipments, but investors appear to be reassessing whether current valuations are justified by repeatable industrial demand. The pullback also comes as Chinese regulators are reportedly applying more scrutiny to humanoid robot IPO candidates.
articles.companies: ["Unitree Robotics", "Agility Robotics", "Churchill Capital Corp. XI", "1X Technologies", "Apptronik", "Figure", "Boston Dynamics"]
articles.advisor_relevance: The article highlights a key investment issue in physical AI: public-market enthusiasm for humanoid robotics is being tested against revenue quality, deployment repeatability, profitability, and regulatory scrutiny. Unitree’s sharp post-IPO decline suggests that even companies with real sales can face valuation pressure if investors question the durability and source of demand. For advisor conversations, this is a useful example of separating long-term robotics adoption potential from near-term hype, especially in capital-intensive AI markets.

articles.title: DeepSeek AI Released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with 1M Context, FP4 KV Cache, and Cross-Layer Attention Reuse
articles.summary: DeepSeek AI released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with a 1M-token context window, 552B backbone parameters, and 196B additional Engram parameters. The release targets serving bottlenecks created by long-horizon agents, including repeated prefills and KV cache pressure on HBM, SSD capacity, and bandwidth, using techniques such as FP4 KV cache and cross-layer attention reuse.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because long-context and agentic AI workloads are making inference more input-heavy and memory-intensive, increasing the importance of HBM, storage capacity, and bandwidth efficiency. While the article does not provide commercial adoption or financial details, the release highlights ongoing innovation aimed at reducing infrastructure constraints that could shape AI cost curves and supplier demand.

articles.title: AgentServeSim: Serving-System Simulation and Policy Search for LLM Agent Programs
articles.summary: AgentServeSim is a simulator for LLM agent programs that models multi-turn agent execution, tool-call gaps, KV-state retention, routing, and scheduling. The authors validate it against real vLLM deployments across two GPU platforms, Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.1-70B, with mean job-completion-time error around 5%, and use it for automated policy search that modestly improves latency versus hand-written policies.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a technical but relevant signal that production agentic AI will require new serving-system infrastructure beyond standard request-level inference. Better simulation, routing, scheduling, and KV-state management may help enterprises reduce latency and improve GPU efficiency, though the reported gains are modest and the work remains academic rather than a direct commercial announcement.
